440083e7-d0c2-582e-be68-2e0366d38ec9.name: *Mythological Scene* (the Forge of Vulcan?)
440083e7-d0c2-582e-be68-2e0366d38ec9.description:
A painting that was part of a series which was once part of the Royal Palace Collection in Buda. In the inventory the painting is described together with the other pieces as: “school of Rubens, unknown figural composition in richly carved gilt wooden frame”.  
It is on the basis of this description, together with the size, that the four pieces have been identified. The paintings, all purchased by members of the Habsburg family over the centuries, were preserved in the Royal Collection but little is known about the method by which the works were selected, or the family’s preferences concerning the artists. It is only a few years ago that the list of works held in the Royal Collection could be investigated and some of the paintings were identified. The works arrived at the Budapest History Museum in poor condition and it is only thanks to exhibitions in recent years that a few of them have been restored.

44ff5030-1782-52cb-a816-7b58f2d32a22.name: The *Mass of Saint Gregory*
44ff5030-1782-52cb-a816-7b58f2d32a22.description:
References in Portuguese inventories to the carpets of “Castile” and the “Levant” became progressively more frequent in the first half of the 16th century and coincided with the period when representation of knotted carpets, in the form of Iberian and Turkish carpets, reached its peak in Portuguese painting.  
This fact is owed to the Muslim presence in the Iberian Peninsula. Pre-existing contact with Arab culture, as well as the production of knotted carpets, preceded the arrival of oriental counterparts and restricted their demand in the market. Facing an already-established network of Iberian, Turkish and North African manufacturers, carpet manufactories had to respond to the demands of a society well used to the consumption of exotic luxury goods.  
The *Mass of Saint Gregory* originally constituted one of the panels from the *predella* of an altarpiece in the church of the Convent of São Francisco. The *predella* comprised 16 paintings depicting scenes from the Eucharist. The painting seen here represents a story made popular in the Golden Legend of the moment when Christ reveals himself on the altar to Pope Gregory; Christ responds to Pope Gregory’s prayer for a sign to convince a deacon, who had earlier confronted him with doubts about the doctrine of transubstantiation. In the painting, St. Gregory kneels before the altar on a carpet of Spanish origin. The carpet’s field is filled with octagonal medallions in which stars and quatrefoils are alternately inserted; the border is filled with a pseudo-*kufic* design interwoven with stylised floral motifs.

45320add-79cd-5e4e-a505-b843b89eb3f3.name: *The Green Valley*
45320add-79cd-5e4e-a505-b843b89eb3f3.description:
Educated at the Beaux-Arts in Cairo, Samir Rafi displays some distance from his academic training. In AH 1366 / AD 1946, he co-founded *Le Groupe d'Art contemporain* (Contemporary Art Group) with Egyptians Al Gazzar and Nada. Leading the modern art movement in Egypt, they rejected storytelling, were inspired by local subjects, and simplified their styles. In this bucolic picture the rise of the Nile fertilises the earth.  
  
Through this symbolic scene Rafi combines a common past with a hopeful present at a time in which British troops were withdrawing from the Suez Canal.

The rise of Orientalism caused it to become extremely popular, appearing as the subject of numerous editions, adaptations, etc. In the 19th century, a tale from the collection was staged in one of Paris' most famous theatres (the Théâtre du Châtelet), and, as this image shows, the theatre was redecorated as an "Oriental palace" for the occasion.

4859e54f-5855-587b-935f-40a00ec2c500.name: The Mother of God Axion Estin
4859e54f-5855-587b-935f-40a00ec2c500.description:
These four icons form a set that depicts the Hymn of Axion Estin, as follows:  
  
It is truly meet and right to bless you, O Theotokos,  
Ever-blessed and most-pure mother of our God.  
More honorable than the Cherubim,  
And beyond compare more glorious than the Seraphim,  
Who without corruption gave birth to God the Word,  
True Theotokos, we magnify you.  
  
According to tradition, this hymn was revealed to an elder monk and his disciple before an icon of the Mother of God in the sanctuary of the main church of Karyes on Mount Athos. During an all-night vigil, they were joined by an unknown monk who called himself Gabriel. As he chanted an unfamiliar hymn, the icon of the Mother of God began to glow. The elder asked Gabriel to write down this hymn, so he inscribed the prayer with his finger on a roof tile “as if it were made of wax”. The tablet was sent to Constantinople, while the image was venerated as miracle-working. The revelation is commemorated on June 11, and the icon is celebrated on July 13.
4859e54f-5855-587b-935f-40a00ec2c500.obtention: From the private collection of Jacques Zolotnitzky. Purchased by Gordon Lankton from Ikonen Galerie, Germany, in 2012. Gifted to the Museum of Russian Icons by Gordon Lankton in 2013.
keywords: Allegorical and symbolical figures; Virgin Mary and Child; Religious iconography; Angels
materials: Egg tempera on wood with silver basma

499f5994-2858-5519-8d58-193c2a6b45ee.name: *Jupiter and Semele*
499f5994-2858-5519-8d58-193c2a6b45ee.description:
A diagonal composition of a pair of nudes in dramatic poses, the picture conveys a story from Greek mythology retold by Ovid in the third volume of *Metamorphoses*. Semele, daughter of Cadmus, the founder of Thebes, tricked by jealous Hera who wants to spoil Zeus's (Jupiter's) philandering, gets Jupiter to grant her wish that he should visit her in his true shape. Saddened, Zeus takes on his divine form, summoning clouds, rain, storm and gale, thunderbolts and lightning. Mortal Semele cannot withstand the raging elements and perishes. Her son Bacchus (Dionysus), conceived earlier, survives, as Zeus sews him into his thigh and carries the future god of wine to full term himself.  
From late renaissance onwards, Ovid's texts were recommended to artists as a wellspring of subjects and were published in a number of illustrated editions. Themes derived from mythology frequently decorated studies and whole mansions. The most popular included erotic scenes, particularly Zeus (Jupiter) visiting his lovers in various shapes, transformed into animals, elements or simple mortals.  
The painted frame of the picture suggests that the canvas was part of an interior decoration, the location for which is as yet unknown. The colour scheme, based on contrasts between blue and red, illuminated by the scale of light, and the peachy tones used for the anatomically elaborate nudes, also has a decorative nature. In addition, it underlines the psychological effect of the bodies portrayed. The discovery of two preparatory sketches in the collection of the State Science Library, Olomouc, allows speculation as to Moravian provenance for the picture. During the period 1691–95 Pagani worked in Kroměříž, Mikulov and on the Velehrad basilica. He probably left for Cracow with the B. Fontana workshop and returned to Italy via Olomouc.

The painted frame of the picture suggests that the canvas was part of an interior decoration, the location for which is as yet unknown.

49ea5362-039b-5261-908a-c40c047fa0bb.name: Turkman Prisoner
49ea5362-039b-5261-908a-c40c047fa0bb.short_description: The Turkoman prisoner is a common subject in Iranian art. The motif was copied and subtly interpreted in both drawings and paintings, which were probably intended for placement in albums. The prisoner depicted here, as in all such representations, is fettered by a *palahang*, a device made from a forked branch, to which one wrist is attached by an additional band of wood or metal. A crossbar at the back of the prisoner’s neck completes the restraint. As is typical, the prisoners’ physiognomy and clothes denote his Turkman ethnicity. He wears a sleeveless outer robe over a long-sleeved tunic, with an elaborately knotted sash; his head is covered by a peaked cap. Characteristically, he carries a sheathed sword, a dagger, a quiver with arrows, a bow and case, a flail, and a whip. Not surprising, given his extensive armaments, he does not seem humbled by his captivity; rather, apart from the introduction of the shackling yoke, such prisoner figures are often nearly indistinguishable from contemporaneous paintings of similarly clothed and armed Uzbek princes or warriors. Based on the Persian poetry by Amir Shahi of Sabzavar (d. 857/1453), which surrounds the painting, it is possible to suggest a less literal meaning for this prisoner imagery. The verses give voice to the torments of unrequited love, a common theme in classical Persian poetry. Claiming to haunt the street of the beloved by night, the lover moans, "Happy is that prisoner who has someone to come to his rescue," which is inscribed, almost like a caption beneath the bent leg of the captive.
49ea5362-039b-5261-908a-c40c047fa0bb.holder: Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA)
49ea5362-039b-5261-908a-c40c047fa0bb.dates: Hegira second half of 10th century / AD second half of 16th century
49ea5362-039b-5261-908a-c40c047fa0bb.method_for_datation: The motif of the Turkman prisoner first appears in Persian painting around the middle of the sixteenth century. The LACMA painting is very similar to one in a Persian-made album in the Topkapi Palace Library, Istanbul, H. 2156, which has margins dated between Hegira 980 / AD 1572 and Hegira 982 /AD 1575. This strong similarity suggests that a tracing was made from the Topkapi version, perhaps datable to the 1560s to early 1570s, which was reversed and used as pounce to produce the LACMA painting.
49ea5362-039b-5261-908a-c40c047fa0bb.method_for_provenance: The motif of the Turkman prisoner is known primarily in Safavid painting; a few instances occur in Mughal India.

4a617bed-3c19-5563-b98a-4cd98cda144d.description: This painting was made around 1863 when the author travelled to Morocco with Mariano Fortuny. During his travels he brought exotic artworks as Egyptian sarcophagi.

4bc8852b-4eb9-5ea3-a533-cfbbadd4a2f8.name: *Coronation Of Tsar Dušan*
4bc8852b-4eb9-5ea3-a533-cfbbadd4a2f8.short_description: *The Coronation of Tsar Dušan* was painted on commission from the Kingdom of Serbia for the 1900 Paris Exposition. Jovanović began to prepare for it two years ahead, taking trips and gathering material in Vienna (Habsburg Court Library), Constantinople, Venice, Skopje, Kosovo and Metohija (Gračanica Monastery). Jovanović's consultant in the creation of this piece was the renowned Serbian historian Stojan Novaković. The artist used the *plein air* (outdoor) painting technique fashionable at the time, one of the reasons being the wish of the commissioning party, more specifically King Milan Obrenović, that Jovanović produce a work suitable for crafting a large tapestry. The painting was unveiled at the 1900 Paris Exposition, drawing flattering recognition and praise and winning a gold medal. The artist was somewhat unhappy with the choice of painting technique, and repeated the subject of Tsar Dušan's coronation (or the Proclamation of Dušan's Code, as it was called for a time after World War II) on numerous occasions after the Paris Expo, in various formats, in different ways and for various purposes until late in life. The fact that there are more than ten replicas and variants by the author himself known to date, speaks of how much this work was esteemed and sought after.
4bc8852b-4eb9-5ea3-a533-cfbbadd4a2f8.author: Petar Petrovic
keywords: Historical Painting

4bccb3e9-a964-52ef-937f-7a6d6e11e5cf.name: *Interior of a house in Boussaada*
4bccb3e9-a964-52ef-937f-7a6d6e11e5cf.short_description: This painting, showing the interior of a traditional house in the Boussaada region, elicits a certain intimacy, recalling the muted atmosphere also evoked by Guillaumet's *Fileuse*. The nervous, moving brushstrokes and his use of melted or soldered lead are clear references to the style of the Dutch masters.
4bccb3e9-a964-52ef-937f-7a6d6e11e5cf.author: Dalila Orfali
keywords: Orientalism

4bd11f30-7eb1-584b-9175-3069c058941f.name: A pair of still-life paintings: Confectionery and Pottery and Confectionery and Flowers
4bd11f30-7eb1-584b-9175-3069c058941f.description:
This is one of two still-life paintings belonging to the Anselmo Braamcamp Freire collection by Josefa d' Óbidos. The influence of the Flemish, Dutch and Andalusian schools, which Josefa d' Óbidos adapted to her Naturalist genre to create her own distinct style, is clearly visible here. The painting reveals an essential simplicity, in which the central details are the confectionary, the pottery and flowers, and it is this very simplicity allied to the artist's delicate technique as well as a wide colour palette, that transform these works into silent and realistic worlds of living objects in all their serenity.  
It is worth mentioning the use of a range of whites which in its subtlety adds to the vivid realism of the paintings and heightens the awakening of all five senses that is so redolent of Baroque Art and so characteristic of this artist.  
Another approach to these paintings is to regard them as allegories of Christianity and the monastic life. Symbols such as the bread, the silverware and the pots are connected to festive occasions and feasts like the Eucharist. Ceramics are associated with the daily rituals of the town of Óbidos.  
It is also possible to establish a connection with the Baroque discourse of the Counter-Reformation in which the gesture and behavioural excesses of human nature stand out, in contrast to the principles and values of purity and simplicity. Valuable objects and luxurious embroideries are represented together with white roses, representing the spirit of patience and red roses, associated with spiritual martyrdom.  
Exploiting her knowledge of symbols and the significance of plants, the artist turns each detail into a symbol of reality and man's moral and spiritual values. Thus, the cherries and roses symbolise happiness, maternal love is suggested by the carnations and eternal life is characterised by the butterfly.
4bd11f30-7eb1-584b-9175-3069c058941f.short_description: Josefa d’ Óbidos' still-life evokes the Counter-Reformation's Baroque ideas in which Man's gesture and behavioural excesses contrast with purity and simplicity. Details like bread, cakes, silver and embroidery symbolise human values in contrast to the flowers, representing spiritual values.
4bd11f30-7eb1-584b-9175-3069c058941f.holder: Museum and House of Anselmo Braamcamp Freire

4bf6a5a2-2ef7-5efd-930f-e900942ddaa6.name: *La Péri: thirteen costume sketches*
4bf6a5a2-2ef7-5efd-930f-e900942ddaa6.short_description: *La Péri* is a fantastical ballet in two acts with the scenario written by Theophile Gautier and the music by Burgmüller. This ballet, first performed in 1843, brought the audience to a grand Egyptian palace. Théophile Gautier dreamt of visiting Egypt, where his friend Gerard de Nerval had been living and sending him details to help him make the ballet more realistic.
keywords: Dance; Orientalism

4c3f617a-7e2c-59e0-b879-f12b80b2aac8.name: *Allegory of Autumn*
4c3f617a-7e2c-59e0-b879-f12b80b2aac8.description: This painting is part of a series representing the *Four Seasons*. It was painted by Pier Francesco Cittadini, a Milanese artist who was a follower of Guido Reni of Bologna. The cycle is described by the eighteenth-century art historian Luigi Crespi in his book *Felsina Pittrice*, printed in 1769. At that time, it was the property of a noble Bolognese family, the Counts Legnani. *Spring* and *Summer* are today housed in the Galleria Estense in Modena; *Winter* and *Autumn* hang together in the same room in the Collezioni Comunali d'Arte in Bologna. Wreaths of fruit and vegetables frame landscapes with mythological scenes connected with the seasons. *Autumn* is symbolised by Bacchus with a vine wreath on his head and a thyrsus in his hand. On the right a drunken Silenus lays down next to a vat. Vine-shoots, pumpkins and pomegranates frame the scene. Cittadini learned this kind of composition, a mixture of still life, mythological scenes and landscape, typical of Flemish painters, during his stay in Rome.
4c3f617a-7e2c-59e0-b879-f12b80b2aac8.short_description: This painting is part of a series depicting the *Four Seasons* painted for the Counts Legnani of Bologna. It is the work of Pier Francesco Cittadini, a Milanese painter celebrated for his still lives and portraits. Bacchus, supervising the wine-making process personifies the allegory of Autumn; a wreath of seasonal fruit, following the Flemish tradition, frames the scene.
4c3f617a-7e2c-59e0-b879-f12b80b2aac8.method_for_datation: The series of the *Four Seasons* is generally connected for stylistic reasons with the garlands of flowers and fruit painted by Cittadini for the Ducal palace in Sassuolo (Gallery of Bacchus), a summer residence of the Este family, where he worked from 1650.
4c3f617a-7e2c-59e0-b879-f12b80b2aac8.obtention: This painting together with its pendant, *Winter*, entered the municipal collections in 1930, through the bequest of Marquis Pier Ignazio Rusconi.

4d147eaa-e780-5bd5-bc8d-41ec30b458e3.name: *Celebration of the Virgin Mary*
4d147eaa-e780-5bd5-bc8d-41ec30b458e3.description: This *tondo* (circular painting) is the design for a ceiling painting in the Czenstochowa Chapel in the Premonstratensian Abbey of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary in Brno–Zábrdovice. The composition consists of a host of saints in discussion, arranged in circles that are increasingly illuminated towards the centre of the picture. The artist has enhanced the illusion of space by partially covering the framing balustrade with vast clouds that provide pedestals for female figures, some of which bear Marian symbols. Behind them is another circular layer of cloud, regularly interrupted by smaller groups of figures. The composition culminates in a dove, the Holy Spirit, depicted in an open vista, the central light source of the picture. Etgens placed the dove – slightly shifted away from centre – above God the Father, the most important figure in the painting. St. Luke is represented as an artist with his attributes: a palette and brushes. From the 10th century onwards, the oldest representation of the Virgin Mary was ascribed to St. Luke and linked to a Marian picture of Hodgetiria type on the altar of the Zábrdovice Chapel, executed as one of many replicas of the Madonna of Czenstochowa. The fact that Christ is missing in the ceiling fresco, but appears as a child with Madonna in the altarpiece, is evidence that the decoration of the chapel was approached as an artistic and compositional whole. The dove of the Holy Spirit and God the Father, with a group of angels making up his pedestal in the original sketch, were intended to be connected with a future painting of the Madonna of Czenstochowa, supplemented within the architecture of the altar by Anton Schweigl's sculpted decoration. Comparison between the colour scheme of the circular picture, in cloudy brown and red tones with bright colour accents, and the ceiling painting is not possible due to extensive damage and restoration work carried out on the latter.
4d147eaa-e780-5bd5-bc8d-41ec30b458e3.short_description: The *tondo* is a design for a ceiling painting in the Czenstochowa Chapel in the Premonstratensian Church of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary. The painting, picking up the threads of the Italian *Seicento*, is one of the last works by the renowned Brno artist, Etgens, who is associated with attempting to establish a public art academy in Brno.
4d147eaa-e780-5bd5-bc8d-41ec30b458e3.method_for_datation: The painting is one of the last works by the renowned Brno artist, Etgens, who is said to have studied in Naples under Francesco Solimena. His name is associated with an attempt to establish a public art academy in Brno. That he executed this fresco is mentioned in the sources.
4d147eaa-e780-5bd5-bc8d-41ec30b458e3.obtention: After the Second World War the picture was held in the Picture Gallery, Brno on long-term loan from the Roman Catholic parish office in Brno–Zábrdovice. In 2001 it passed to the Premonstratensian Abbey, Nová Říše, originally located in Zábrdovice.

4d43096d-e741-5b21-a636-ccbb17e263cf.name: *Windows*
4d43096d-e741-5b21-a636-ccbb17e263cf.description:
Wafa al-Hamad’s exploration of doors and windows delves into the intersection of heritage and visual transformation within the Gulf region. These architectural elements, often crafted with precision, symbolise entry and exit-gates to the past, present, and future. Drawing from the historic buildings of Qatar, UAE, and Bahrain, she captures their ornate facades as a means of preserving fading architectural traditions amidst rapid modernization. Her paintings, such as this one, function as portals, inviting viewers into spaces where the past remains alive.  
  
Rooted in Islamic art, al-Hamad’s work frequently incorporates geometric abstraction and calligraphy, though these elements are not present in this piece. In the 1990s (AH 1410), she has additionally woven Arabic proverbs into her compositions, enriching her art with cultural depth. These proverbs serve as visual metaphors, blending the functionality of objects with poetic symbolism and allowing her to explore concepts within a contemporary framework.  
  
"I have developed a strong interest towards these ancestral doors, in their excellent craftsmanship, a sublime beauty, uniqueness and inspirational representation of faith…My paintings convey such meanings especially door panels which truly express what I believe in. Door panels stand at the crossroad of our ancestral heritage. They pave the way to the realm of Islamic art, its form, decorative accents and inscriptions." - Wafa al-Hamad
4d43096d-e741-5b21-a636-ccbb17e263cf.holder: MATHAF, Arab Museum of Modern Art
keywords: watercolour; water; art; window

4d95a12b-05ca-5d85-bfaf-474830773927.name: Monkeys taunting a lion
4d95a12b-05ca-5d85-bfaf-474830773927.short_description: This single-page drawing of Monkeys Taunting a Lion is on a folio from a dispersed album. Ruled off in a pale blue frame decorated with golden trees, flowers, birds, and insects and trimmed down to a narrow frame ornamentation, the drawing is outlined in black and has line detail with some light grey shading. The subject of this drawing is not determined by a narrative text. However, it may have been inspired by an animal fable such as *Kalila wa Dimna* (Kalila and Dimna), which has a long tradition in Iran.\[1\] The artist was also likely influenced by the influx of Chinese styles, patterns, and motifs in the early 15th century.\[2\] The vogue for Chinese drawing and painting may have been the inspiration for this drawing, similar to the wild landscape with the struggling animals and dragon.

4dac9cf9-671a-53db-afe9-db1a23d3b6cf.name: Preparation of Medicine. Folio from Manuscript of an Arabic Translation of 'De Materia Medica' of Dioscorides
4dac9cf9-671a-53db-afe9-db1a23d3b6cf.short_description: This is a single leaf from a manuscript copied in AH 621 / AD 1224 in Baghdad by Abdallah ibn al-Fadl, a well-known calligrapher, for a long time believed to be the author of the miniatures. "De Materia Medica" a treatise by Dioscorides, a Greek doctor, was very popular in the Middle Ages. The Khanenko Museum keeps a folio that depicts a process of medicine-making. Extremely trustworthy and artistically convincing is the manner used by the medieval artist in rendering ethnic features of personages, their gestures, clothing and various details of everyday life.
4dac9cf9-671a-53db-afe9-db1a23d3b6cf.method_for_datation: Stylistic analysis by V. Krachkovskaya (1926, origin), publication of H. Buchthal (1942, accurate date).
4dac9cf9-671a-53db-afe9-db1a23d3b6cf.method_for_provenance: Publication of Vera Krachkovskaya (1927): the Khanenkos' collection, publication of Hugo Buchthal (1942): former Fredrik Robert Martin's collection.
4dac9cf9-671a-53db-afe9-db1a23d3b6cf.obtention: Purchased by Bohdan and Varvara Khanenko in Paris, 1914, from Fredrik Robert Martin's collection. Donated by Varvara Khanenko in 1918, nationalised by Bolshevik regime in 1919.

4dbcd917-010c-5ebd-8b39-646ec4f29059.name: "Bahram Gur Sees a Herd of Deer Mesmerized by Dilaram' s Music"
4dbcd917-010c-5ebd-8b39-646ec4f29059.alternate_name: Folio from a Khamsa (Quintet) of Amir Khusrau Dihlavi
4dbcd917-010c-5ebd-8b39-646ec4f29059.description: Approximately one century after the Persian poet Nizami wrote his Khamsa (Quintet), the Indian poet Amir Khusrau Dihlavi composed a response using Nizami’s structure but varying his stories slightly. This painting comes from the Mughal emperor Akbar’s (r. 1556–1605) personal copy of Amir Khusrau’s verses. It shows the king Bahram Gur with his beautiful slave girl, Dilaram, who could make animals sleep or awaken with the sound of her music.

4de3eb32-b57d-5953-83b6-9b88acb3de21.name: *St. Francis Xavier*
4de3eb32-b57d-5953-83b6-9b88acb3de21.description:
Following liberation from Turkish occupation, the Jesuits were among the first to occupy the prominent towns of northeast Croatia. They arrived in Požega, a town at the very heart of the so-called *Valis Aurea*, the Golden Valley surrounded by mountains, in the middle of the Slavonian plain.  
This painting of St. Francis Xavier was probably among the first artworks installed to decorate the Jesuit College in Požega, built and equipped soon after the Jesuit's arrival in 1698. The pendant to this painting presents the Immaculate Conception in a very specific way, with the Madonna sitting on a throne and the Child standing on a serpent's head next to her.  
*St. Francis Xavier* shows the saint baptising the local inhabitants on one of his missions to the East. The composition is common in works with a similar theme, for example, in the small-size oil painting, the *Baptism of Queen Neachila of India* by the same artist. This work, a kind of study or *bozzetto*, is in Düsseldorf Museum, while a painting of the same subject on a larger scale is in the Kiscelli Museum, Budapest.  
In the Požega painting, the figure of the saint is notable for its monumental gesture: the almost three-quarter length, front-facing figure of the saint pouring holy water from the small bucket onto the heads of the three figures gathered around the baptismal font. The stunning texture of the paint reveals the author's dynamic gestural brushstrokes. The somewhat cold and distant colours are surprising in a scene supposedly taking place in Asia and Africa, where warmer and more saturated colours are expected. Nevertheless, the specific chromatic values seen here are frequent in Pozzo's paintings, as are the dynamic brushstrokes.
4de3eb32-b57d-5953-83b6-9b88acb3de21.short_description: *St. Francis Xavier* is one of a few easel paintings by the Baroque painter, architect and art theoretician Andrea Pozzo. Brought to Požega by the Jesuits soon after 1698 after liberation from the Ottomans, the stunning detail reveals the author's eloquent gestural brushstrokes.
4de3eb32-b57d-5953-83b6-9b88acb3de21.holder: Diocese Museum of the Požega Diocese
4de3eb32-b57d-5953-83b6-9b88acb3de21.method_for_datation: The date and the origin of this painting were established partly by the *Historia domus* of the Jesuit College in Požega and through comparative analysis of other known works by the same author.
4de3eb32-b57d-5953-83b6-9b88acb3de21.obtention: Originally owned by the Jesuits of Požega, Joseph II confiscated this painting along with the entire Jesuit inventory when he banned the order. Some of the paintings became part of the Diocese Museum of the Zagreb Archdiocese. Shortly after the Požega Diocese was established, the painting was returned to Požega.

4e27b872-ecb5-5764-8ab4-12316b90ca21.name: *Marketplace, Morocco*
4e27b872-ecb5-5764-8ab4-12316b90ca21.short_description: This imposing oil painting shows a caravan apparently leaving the gate of a North African city, perhaps Fez, with much commotion going on on either side of the camels and their guides. Although the title of the painting suggest a market scene, in reality little trading activity can be seen apart from an old hooded man sitting next to a large basket with shoes on the right. On the left a group of African men and a little child in a burnous admire the skills of a snake charmer, while his monkey next to him looks on intently. In the background, large numbers of men, apparently both of Arab and Berber origin, and dressed in a variety of traditional dress, walk along or stand together in groups conversing, oblivious to the camels, donkeys and horses moving inbetween them. Ferenc Eisenhut was an Austro-Hungarian painter, known for his monumentally conceived genre scenes of Eastern life and vistas. He was the only internationally acclaimed, Hungarian Orientalist painter.
4e27b872-ecb5-5764-8ab4-12316b90ca21.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
4e27b872-ecb5-5764-8ab4-12316b90ca21.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis

4e299372-2148-578c-ac70-4b781a5ad8ce.name: *The First Train in Spain: Inaugurated 28 October 1848*
4e299372-2148-578c-ac70-4b781a5ad8ce.description: The railway connecting Barcelona and Mataró was the first one to be inaugurated in Spain. This train connected two important industrial hubs of Catalonia, as an example of the industrial development of this area in the middle of the 19th century.

keywords: Railways; Spain

4efddfdd-e8a3-5895-9f9c-d7247e51a06f.name: Portrait of an unknown scholar
4efddfdd-e8a3-5895-9f9c-d7247e51a06f.short_description:
This portrait depicts a calligrapher or scholar, wearing a white turban and with a red beard dyed with henna. Crouched in the corner of a simple room, lost in thought, he holds the mouthpiece of his water pipe. To his left, on top of a chest, a few personal objects include a pair of spectacles, a silver pocket watch, pencil cases, a book and a small glass vase with a bunch-flowered narcissus (*Narcissus tazetta*).  
  
We know almost nothing about the painter, Mirza Aqa, mentioned in the poem accompanying this portrait. The qualities of this work are due in particular to the pictorial technique used by the painter. The faithful, almost rough rendering of the face gives the figure a strong, penetrating presence. The play of perspective, light and shadow, and the realism shown by the painter can be found in other contemporary Qajar painters.

4f180fa5-704f-5c7d-ae79-fb6f43f46920.name: Reverse glass painting: *Vulcan surprises Venus*
4f180fa5-704f-5c7d-ae79-fb6f43f46920.description: The reverse glass painting by the Zurich artist Hans Conrad Gyger depicts the dramatic moment when Vulcan, the god of fire, steps into the sleeping chamber and catches his wife Venus in the amorous embrace of Mars. From the clouds above the Olympian gods witness the divine adultery. The theme’s composition – otherwise rarely depicted in Swiss reverse glass painting – traces back to the Zurich artist Gotthard Ringgli who gave Gyger two sketches with detailed studies of the two lovers. Ringgli, in turn, was relying on a Dutch drawing as his template. Possibly the precious work was created as a wedding present, with the intention of reminding the future couple of conjugal fidelity. Who commissioned the work is not known. The signature of Hans Conrad Gyger on the dark chest in the foreground was only discovered in 1997 in the context of restoration work. Until then Gyger had been famous above all for his cartographic work and, according to Joachim Sandrat, for a special procedure he developed for decorating glass objects with oil paints. Using this technique he decorated pictures, drinking vessels and mirrors, gaining popularity well beyond Zurich, as far as Paris, Florence and Venice.
4f180fa5-704f-5c7d-ae79-fb6f43f46920.method_for_datation: In 1997, during restauration, the Signature of Hans Conrad Gyger was discovered. The Date is also inscribed on the painting.
4f180fa5-704f-5c7d-ae79-fb6f43f46920.obtention: The painting was part of the private collection of Heinrich Angst, the first Director of the Landesmuseum and was later (1907) bought by the Landesmuseum.
keywords: painting; reverse glass painting; Roman mythology; Venus; Mars; Vulcan; adultery; Hans Conrad Gyger
materials: Glass, reverse painted, verre églomisé; tin foil

4f6d8c3a-63e3-50c0-b243-faaa3ddd2001.name: *The Expulsion of the Duke of Athens*
4f6d8c3a-63e3-50c0-b243-faaa3ddd2001.short_description: The painting is a second version by the artist of his masterpiece *La cacciata del Duca di Atene* started by Ussi in 1854 in Rome and finished in Florence, now at the National Gallery of Modern Art in Florence. The artwork was presented at the National Exhibition in Florence in 1861 and sent at the International Exhibition in Paris in 1867 where it was awarded the silver medal. The scene depicted in the painting refers to the book *Istorie Fiorentine* by Nicolò Machiavelli. In particular the painter shows the moment in which Gualtieri di Brienne, Duke of Athens between 1342-43, abdicates from Florence. To his left are the republicans who force him to sign. The second version is slightly different from the original one in characters and manner. The painting shows the city of Florence, represented by the republicans, defending its freedom from a cruel ruler and embodies a strong political, civic and moral relevance, emphasised by the sheer size of the canvas.

50900128-bb54-580c-9129-d9d24be9c5ef.name: Ten folios from the *Shahnamah* of Firdawsi made for Shah Tahmasp I
50900128-bb54-580c-9129-d9d24be9c5ef.short_description:
The ten folios come the *Shahnamah* made for the Safavid ruler, Shah Tahmasp I (r. 1524–1576). One of the finest illustrated Persian manuscript ever made, it has been referred to as the ‘Houghton’ *Shahnamah* after the collector who broke it up in New York in the 1970s. It is of large format, on fine gold-sprinkled paper, and with 258 illustrations. The format is independently conceived for each painting and must have involved constant consultation between scribes, painters and marginators. Folio 516, which in the Khalili Collection, is the only folio in the manuscript to bear a date.  
The manuscript was given by Shah Tahmasp to the Ottoman Sultan Selim II at the time of the latter’s accession in 1566. By 1903, the manuscript was in the possession of Edmond de Rothschild. It changed hands once again in the 1960s, when its then owner, Arthur Houghton Jr, began to disperse it. Today, some 140 of its paintings are in museums and collections throughout the world. The rest of the manuscript – the binding, the text block and 118 paintings – have been in the Contemporary Art Museum in Tehran since 1994.

52a99ada-0675-50d5-a178-836792f337d3.name: *The Virgin at the Nile*
52a99ada-0675-50d5-a178-836792f337d3.short_description: Federico Faruffini made his debut as a painter at the 1856 annual exposition of Brera. In his works the artist breaks away from the academic rule of ‘disegno’, or artistic drawing, and focuses on colour. The painting *The Virgin at the Nile* shows a sacrifice. Numerous study sketches survive. They attest that the artist was well educated on customs, traditions and architecture of ancient Egypt. In the painting the artist proposes the integration of two separate themes through different rendering styles: on the brighter upper part he sets the historic characters and in the lower zone the more narrative one, of obvious academic inspiration. The painting was brought to Paris by the artist after he decided to leave Italy because he was having difficulty finding work. After the artist committed suicide, *The Virgin at the Nile* was on display at the retrospective exhibition in Rome in 1883 where Faruffini’s entire portfolio was reconsidered, and the painting was declared his undiscussed masterpiece.

52e50179-8187-524b-bf97-e2dc4d14855d.name: 'Saz'-style drawing of a dragon amid foliage
52e50179-8187-524b-bf97-e2dc4d14855d.short_description: The mid‑sixteenth century saw the flourishing of the so‑called *saz* style—characterized by the depiction of stylised, serrated leaf foliage, often paired with fantastic creatures including dragons and phoenixes. This imagery appears on Ottoman art in a variety of media, including textiles. This magnificent dragon drawing is ascribed to the master of the style, Shah Quli, an artist who emigrated from Iran to Istanbul and became head of the royal atelier under Sultan Süleyman the Magnificent.

54a75fca-9a38-5dc2-9f8e-80faf09f8470.name: *The Artist Girl and Her Studio*
54a75fca-9a38-5dc2-9f8e-80faf09f8470.short_description: The basis of Turkish painting drawing influence from western tradition was laid when *Mühendishane-i Berr-i Hümayun* (the Naval Academy) opened in 1795. Halil Pasha, who had been a student of the painting courses held at the Academy, was foremost among the painters with a military background who founded a western style art tradition in Turkey. He worked with Jean Leon Gerome in his atelier in Paris. He provided a unique distinction to the analysis of impressionist light and colour, and was an example of artists dealing with impressionist technique. Because of his qualified knowledge about anatomy and his interest in depicting the human figure, Halil Pasha had a unique place in Turkish Art History.
keywords: Painting; Halil Pasha; orientalist Turkish painters

555612b1-3b0e-5939-af4c-dcd61c208ab2.name: *Reading The Qu'ran*
555612b1-3b0e-5939-af4c-dcd61c208ab2.short_description: Osman Hamdi focused on dilemmas such as East and West, love and hate, life and death. While stylistically reminiscent of western Orientalist painters, his works reflect a more nuanced appreciation of Ottoman society and culture. He also gave importance to details while reflecting the colourful scenes of Turkish culture, traditional architecture, Ottoman fashion and domestic and social life of the women in the Ottoman Empire. And it’s obvious that he is the first painter who used human figures in the western style.
keywords: Painting; Osman Hamdi Bey; orientalist Turkish painters

5599db05-ed21-5635-bc98-8d9bcd6907e1.name:
Album page  
Front, Emperor Jahangir at the *jharoka* window  
Back, calligraphy
5599db05-ed21-5635-bc98-8d9bcd6907e1.short_description: This double-sided page, intended for an album, is likely the product of two masters: Abu‘l-Hasan, one of the most famous artists of the Mughal court, and Muhammad Husayn al-Kashmiri, honoured by the emperor Akbar (r. 1556–1605) with the title of 'Zarin Qalam' (Golden Pen). \[1\] The painting depicts Emperor Jahangir (r. 1605–27) in a balcony window (called a *jharoka*) and looking down to Agra Fort. His top-ranking officials stand on the marble terrace just below him. Beneath the terrace, lower-ranking officials and the public gather in a courtyard. Near the red canopy at the left is suspended a golden chain with golden bells.

5647174a-d70c-5acf-8ebd-27ca4e8179a6.name: *St. Barbara*
5647174a-d70c-5acf-8ebd-27ca4e8179a6.description:
This half-figure of a woman holding a palm frond suggests a Christian martyr; the chalice, communion wafer, sword and tower in the background help identify her as St. Barbara, the patron saint of miners, artillerymen, gunsmiths and all who work with explosives. Legend has it that her father, a pagan nobleman, had a tower erected to imprison his daughter and discourage prospective suitors. The tower had only two windows. In her father’s absence, Barbara persuaded workers to add a third window. She also had a priest visit in secret and baptise her. When her father returned, Barbara explained that the three windows symbolised the Holy Trinity illuminating her soul. The father turned her over to the Roman authorities. When Barbara refused to abandon her faith, she was tortured and finally decapitated.  
The monochrome colour scheme, light contrasts and the artist’s original handwriting hint at inspiration by Dutch and Flemish 17th-century painting. The smoothly arched face contrasts with the relaxed rendering of the drapery. The portrait features of the saint suggest an interest in individual psychology, and embody a crypto-portrait of the artist’s wife.  
Willmann was probably apprenticed to his father’s workshop before leaving for the Netherlands. It has been maintained that he was a direct student of Rembrandt; he certainly came into contact with Rembrandt’s art and was allegedly in touch with Jacob de Backer, a student of Rembrandt, as well as with a circle of landscape artists around Jacob van Ruisdael. In Antwerp, he became acquainted with the work of Rubens and Van Dyck. The painter later moved to Breslau where his work attracted the interest of the Cistercian abbot of the Lubiaz monastery. The artist joined his service and settled in Lubiaz for good, painting for the abbey and other monasteries in Bohemia and Moravia. His stay was only broken by a trip to the Elector’s court in Berlin, where he was appointed court painter.

The smoothly arched face contrasts with the relaxed rendering of the drapery. The portrait features of the saint embody a crypto-portrait of the artist’s wife.

56d6cbbe-5568-5bd2-85e4-4918e6039102.name: Youth in a Fur Trimmed Cap
56d6cbbe-5568-5bd2-85e4-4918e6039102.short_description: In sixteenth-century Iran, single-page paintings became popular. These were cheaper to produce and hence cheaper to purchase than were manuscripts containing many illustrations. Most common were images of aristocratic youths, standing alone, carefully executed and fully coloured, such as this example from about 1600, which is the work of Riza Abbasi, who has signed the painting at the lower left. The plump young man clutches a bottle, probably a wine-flask. His fur hat is exquisitely rendered and he sports a magnificent pair of patterned trousers.
keywords: Painting
materials: Coloured pigments and gold on paper

572d0642-eeed-51ff-b840-e50c47614c23.name: Reverse painting on glass: The Arab hero Abdallah Ibn Jaafar and the Christian princess Yamina
572d0642-eeed-51ff-b840-e50c47614c23.short_description: As Tunisia fell under French rule in 1881, reverse paintings on glass were fashionable in Tunis and Sfax. The story of Abdallah and Princess Yamina was beloved. In 647, the first onslaught of Muslim Arabs reached the Byzantine province of Africa. Near today's city of Sbeïtla, they scored a decisive victory over the Eastern Roman commander-in-chief Gregorius. The event embedded itself deeply in the collective consciousness of the population, and at the time of the French Protectorate it was again unearthed. An image shows the Arab hero Abdallah ibn Jaafar and the Christian Princess Yamina fleeing on horseback. The pair miraculously saved themselves from the Eastern Roman pursuers. Abdallah kidnapped an infidel, conquered the enemy and wounded his dignity. Around 1900, this pictorial image was commonly displayed between Tunis and Algiers as a visual protest against the French colonial powers.
572d0642-eeed-51ff-b840-e50c47614c23.method_for_datation: Entry in the general inventory and archival documents.

5742022d-5251-5bf2-9309-1b5f081234cd.short_description: Until the 19th century, Portuguese painting focussed on landscape and local habits. The new interest for travelling and for other cultures can be seen in this oil painting by Silva Porto portraying a girl from the Island of Capri and her costume.

574d6f3c-2cbb-5d5b-9f00-e0dd275b71a9.name: *Excavation of the Great Temple of Ramesses II at Abu Simbel*
574d6f3c-2cbb-5d5b-9f00-e0dd275b71a9.short_description:
An intrepid and versatile Frenchman, Linant came to Egypt in 1818. In Cairo he adopted the life of an Ottoman Turk, but was known and consulted by European residents and visitors as well as by the Pasha of Egypt, Muhammad Ali. At various times his talents were employed as a geographer, explorer, engineer, cartographer and draughtsman.  
His first adventure was an expedition to Upper Egypt that Henry Salt, British Consul-General in Egypt , took to Abu Simbel in 1818-19. Although there were other artists in the party it is likely that this watercolour is by Linant and that it depicts Salt's attempts to clear away the ever encroaching sand from the facade of the Great Temple. Linant took part in several subsequent expeditions up the Nile, and was one of the first Europeans to reach the Pharaonic sites of Meroe and Musawarat.
574d6f3c-2cbb-5d5b-9f00-e0dd275b71a9.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
keywords: Pasha; Salt; Suez

577527f6-207f-54b6-8eee-af77d7cc4100.name:
Shah Faridun spurning the peace envoys of Salm and Tur  
Folio detached from a *Shahnameh* (Book of Kings) by Abu’l-Qasim Firdausi (d. 1010)
577527f6-207f-54b6-8eee-af77d7cc4100.short_description: Recounting the legendary history of Iran’s shahs (kings) up to the Arab conquest in 642 AD and the country’s adoption of Islam, Firdausi’s epic poem the *Shahnameh* (Book of Kings), completed in 1010, inspired many illustrated copies. The present folio depicting Shah Faridun spurning the peace envoys of Salm and Tur was detached from a copy that is known as the “Big Head” *Shahnameh*. This name refers to the characteristic feature of the majority of its paintings: the large heads of its human figures.

materials: Opaque watercolour, gold and ink on paper

57d9ec8b-2100-527f-abb2-8188927bef19.name: *The Gate of a Mosque, Istanbul*
57d9ec8b-2100-527f-abb2-8188927bef19.short_description: This oil painting shows the entrance gate to an Ottoman mosque or mausoleum complex, set in a lush shaded garden with majestic trees, its tall pointed minaret soaring high above the tiled awnings of the surrounding wall. Two turbaned old men, one seated on the pavement at the gate, the other standing to face him, accentuate the scene on the street outside. The painter of this somewhat melancholy scene, Halil Bey, was trained under Gerome and Courtoix. Under the influence of European artists and encouraged by the tastes of the Ottoman court, the arts underwent a great deal of transformation in the 13th/ 19th century. Painting in western styles gained increasing acceptance, and several local artists now concentrated on depicting their surroundings in a manner and style which they had learned in painting and drawing classes given by European instructors, either in Ottoman cities, or - as in the case of Halil Bey - in the prominent European centres of art.

58119adb-f72f-58c9-af23-ed78c51ccea1.name: *Sita Shies Away from Hanuman, Believing He is Ravana in Disguise*
58119adb-f72f-58c9-af23-ed78c51ccea1.short_description: The Great Mughal Akbar was known for his religious tolerance, and he did what he could to give his fellow Muslims insight into Hindu culture. He had holy Hindu scriptures translated into Persian, and he presented the magnificent copy of the *Ramayana* from which this miniature comes to his mother in 1594.

5a5065ff-617c-5f77-81aa-546635c333e8.name: *Saint Charles Borromeo Administers the Sacrament to the Plague-Infected*
5a5065ff-617c-5f77-81aa-546635c333e8.description:
This excellent oil sketch (*bozzetto*) is linked to one of Caspar Franz Sambach's early works, the interior decoration of the parish church in Sloup, Moravia, a grand ensemble of magnificent frescoes and altarpieces, which were completed between 1751 and 1754. The Esztergom *bozzetto*, and a slightly larger and more complete version in Breslau (Wrocław; the Narodowe Museum), were produced for the side altarpiece dedicated to St. Charles Borromeo. The composition follows Pierre Mignard's painting for the high altar of the Church of San Carlo ai Catinari in Rome, probably by way of an intermediary engraving.  
Charles Borromeo, the archbishop of Milan at the time of the great plague of 1576, fought heroically against the epidemic; following his canonisation in 1612, he was accorded reverence similar to that of the medieval plague saints. His cult outside Milan strengthened in Rome at first, and then, through Borromeo family connections in Salzburg, it grew further during the reign of Charles VI spreading throughout the Habsburg Empire.  
Born in Breslau (Wrocław), according to local studies, Sambach worked in Vienna from 1740 in the workshop of the sculptor Georg Raphael Donner. He trained as a historical painter at the Academy of Fine Arts in Vienna, becoming a member in 1759, a professor in 1762 and director in 1773. His fresco and altarpiece paintings were influenced by other Central European painters, the likes of Paul Troger, Michelangelo Unterberger and the younger Franz Anton Maulbertsch. Sambach was a skilful ornamental artist and painted his own architecture; producing the figure inserts that imitate reliefs on his frescoes, as well as on his canvases depicting *putti,* making use of the methods learned from the works of the Austrian, sculptor Georg Raphael Donner. In Hungary, the high altar and ceiling frescoes, together with the altarpieces of the Jesuit church in Székesfehérvár (1749–50), preserve his early, relaxed style. The Esztergom colour sketch, a loose and vivid composition that shows only the lower part of the altarpiece, can be considered as an autograph version (*ricordo*) made by the master.
5a5065ff-617c-5f77-81aa-546635c333e8.short_description: The Silesian, Caspar Franz Sambach, also worked in Hungary (Székesfehérvár, Buda and Nagykanizsa). One of his most important works is the interior decoration in the parish church in Sloup, Moravia, including the altarpiece commemorating Charles Borromeo. Two oil sketches of Charles Borromeo's altarpiece are extant; the one seen here is considered to be an autograph version (*ricordo*) of the Breslau (Wrocław) study.

5a8a244d-67e0-5d59-8dde-4569de053291.name: *General Junot Protecting the City of Lisbon*
5a8a244d-67e0-5d59-8dde-4569de053291.description:
In the context of the French invasions of Portugal Domingos Sequeira established friendships with the officers of the Napoleonic army at an early stage, as was the case with Count Forbin, an officer and amateur painter. Due to these contacts Sequeira was commissioned to produce an allegorical painting to celebrate the role of General Junot in protecting the city of Lisbon. Sequeira's action was perceived as an acceptance of the ideals of the occupying enemy and he was persecuted and his work condemned. Later on, after the defeat of the French, it was difficult for Sequeira to exonerate himself, something that has still only partially been achieved.  
Three groups in the open-air on the top of a hill populate the foreground. Standing in the main central group is General Junot who wears military uniform and is turned towards a young woman who represents Lisbon; she is supported by Religion and Genius of the Nation. To the left in the mid-ground are two men; with only their bare torsos visible they represent Mars annihilating Neptune, and symbolise France and England respectively. On the opposite side, two female figures suspended mid-air move towards the central group; they represent Ceres and Minerva and are symbols of Abundance and Wisdom. Above them an eagle hovers, its huge wings outspread. The landscape is a great plain that stretches out until it reaches the sea. At mid-distance, a large army with knights on horseback advance in formation. In the background a fleet is anchored near the beach. The sky, heavy with clouds, creates a gloom that covers the greater part of the painting. The sky opens out, however, to clearer and more luminous tonality towards the horizon over the sea.
5a8a244d-67e0-5d59-8dde-4569de053291.short_description: The French General, Junot, offers protection to the city of Lisbon, supported by the personifications of Religion and Genius of the Nation. The central composition is flanked by Mars and Neptune (representing France and England) and on the opposite side, Ceres and Minerva under a huge figure of an eagle.

5b990d35-bcaf-52cf-a880-52eebc5cded0.name: *Zulaikha Seizing the Skirt of Yusuf's Robe* Folio from an album (or manuscript) with ghazals by Sa'adi
5b990d35-bcaf-52cf-a880-52eebc5cded0.short_description:
The miniature on the folio illustrates one of the key episodes of the poem "Yusuf and Zuleikha" by Jami. Zuleikha invites Yusuf (pictured with a “flame of the prophet" around his head) to a magnificent palace where he declares love. However, the virtuous Yusuf tries to escape. Zuleikha catches up to him at the door and grabs the edge of his robe. The man in the golden crown watching the scene from behind the open door on the left is probably the husband of Zulayaha, the Egyptian nobleman. He holds a "finger of surprise" at his mouth - a conditional gesture in Persian miniature signifying great astonishment.  
The composition and style of the painting follow a famous miniature of AD 1640, attributed to the brush of Muin Musavvir (1617–1702), an outstanding master of the Isfahan painting school.  
Interestingly, the miniature is painted on a folio from a poetic album (or a manuscript) of the late 16th century, containing poems by Sa’adi Shirazi (1203 / 1210–1291), a great Persian poet.

5c13ad64-b549-5470-8c28-60447c1829ab.name: Christ in Majesty
5c13ad64-b549-5470-8c28-60447c1829ab.description: This icon, known as Christ in Majesty, was once part of the Deesis tier as well as the centerpiece of an iconostasis, a wall of icons separating the nave from the sanctuary in an Orthodox church. An icon of the Mother of God would have hung to the right and an icon of John the Baptist to the left. The Deesis tier usually extends outward on either side with Archangels Michael and Gabriel and the apostles facing Christ. This image represents Christ’s Second Coming and Last Judgment. He is seated on a throne surrounded by seraphim and cherubim angels in a scene of glory based on visions of the Old Testament prophets. Christ’s radiance illuminates the whole scene. The corners depict the symbols of the four evangelists, Matthew, Mark, Luke and John. Christ bestows a blessing with his right hand and in his left holds the Bible open to the passage, “Come to me all ye that labor and are heavy laden and I will give you rest” (Matthew 11:28-29). The Greek letters in three sections of Christ’s halo represent the oneness of the three-part Trinity. At the very top of this icon are the letters IC and XC, representing the first and last initials of the Greek name for Jesus Christ.
5c13ad64-b549-5470-8c28-60447c1829ab.obtention: Purchased by Gordon Lankton from the Temple Gallery, London, in 2009. Gifted by Gordon Lankton to the Museum of Russian Icons in 2013.
keywords: Jesus Christ; Religious iconography; Allegorical and symbolical figures; Angels

5c505fce-a478-511a-be3a-4ccea6c65fe1.name: An illustrated copy of the *Shahnamah* of Firdawsi
5c505fce-a478-511a-be3a-4ccea6c65fe1.short_description:
This copy of Firdawsi’s epic is richly illustrated with 62 paintings, most extending well beyond the rulings. Stylistically, the paintings are the work of at least four artists, but only three of them are signed by Kazim Quli, who is otherwise unrecorded.  
According to the colophon on folio 541a, the copying of the text was completed on 14 September 1602. No patron is mentioned, but a note on folio 1a, written by the Mughal emperor Jahangir, mentions that the manuscript entered the Mughal royal library on 21 March 1609. The manuscript remained there until at least 25 April 1686, as attested by a number of inspection and transfer notes on folios 1a and 541b, written by librarians during the reigns of emperors Jahangir, Shah Jahan and Awrangzeb. A note on folio 1a, accompanied by the names of 3 witnesses, mentions that the manuscript was in Shikarpur on 10 September 1739, when it was given to a certain Haji ‘Abbas who was to hand it over to Sardar Mir Afdal Khan in Qandahar.
5c505fce-a478-511a-be3a-4ccea6c65fe1.holder: Khalili Family Trust – Nasser D. Khalili Collection of Islamic Art
5c505fce-a478-511a-be3a-4ccea6c65fe1.dates: Dated Friday, 27 Rabi‘ al-Awwal 1011 / AD 14 September 1602
5c505fce-a478-511a-be3a-4ccea6c65fe1.method_for_datation: Date and provenance are based on the colophon and the notes written by Mughal emperors and officials within the Mughal royal library.

5cb50de2-2586-516f-843e-945e72d7f294.name: Miniature
5cb50de2-2586-516f-843e-945e72d7f294.description:
In this miniature, an entire world of living beings—mothers and children, animals, plants, and all forms of life—is depicted within a single drop of water. Beneath the drop appears an Arabic inscription from the Qur’an, Surat al-Anbiya (21:30):  
"*Ve ce‘alnā min al-mā’i kulla shay’in ḥayy*" —  
“We created every living thing from water.”  
  
The work symbolises the idea that all beings are bound together through water, sharing a common origin and interdependence. Reflecting this message, the Istanbul Water Museum has embraced the motto “Su Kardeşliği” — "The Brotherhood of Water."
5cb50de2-2586-516f-843e-945e72d7f294.holder: İstanbul Su Müzesi / Istanbul Water Museum
5cb50de2-2586-516f-843e-945e72d7f294.method_for_datation: Date and origin are written on the piece.
5cb50de2-2586-516f-843e-945e72d7f294.author: Ercan Topçu, Barış Topçu
keywords: Water; Qur'an; Miniature

5cd47c3e-f1b1-509d-9ccf-cb760a90b372.name: *Apostle Matthew*
5cd47c3e-f1b1-509d-9ccf-cb760a90b372.description:
The Church and Cloister of the Order of St. Basil in Máriapócs in the Eparchy of Munkács (Mukachevo) was an important centre of the Greek Catholic Church in historical Hungary before the Trianon Peace Treaty of 1920 and the breaking up of the Austro-Hungarian Empire. In this region, the Western Church met with the Eastern churches of the Byzantine ritual, which joined with Rome in 1646. While the 15th and 16th centuries were characterised by the homogeneous Medieval Meta-Byzantine Christian culture of the Eastern churches in the Carpathian region, the 17th century saw modern attitudes surface together with renovation of churches, and the appearance and florescence of a local Late Renaissance style. As the 18th century dawned, a new chapter began in the history of the Eastern churches, one of modernisation, an orientation towards the West and the gradual prevalence of the Baroque.  
Of the iconostases that survive from the second half of the 18th century, the majority were by Galitsian painters, masters from local travelling studios and folk artists. From this time on, Baroque and Rococo features dominated in the style of the icons, as well as the structural elements of the iconostases. Remarkable among these, are works by Mihály (Mihail) and Tádé (Tadeus) Spalinszky. Both originated from Galitzia and became the principal painters of the Eparchy (e.g. the iconostases in Sátoraljaújhely, Ungvár (Uzhorod) and Máriapócs). In 1785, Mihály Spalinszky signed a contract to paint the Máriapócs icons, for which he was paid 130 German Gold coins. The documents relating to the commission are in the Order's archives. This full-figure icon of the Apostle Matthew was isolated from the iconostasis of painted Apostles, all of which were, presumably, after Baroque engravings and painted by the artist Mihály Spalinszky from Galitzia.  
Alongside icons, the Greek Catholic Church and the Eparchy of Munkács (Mukachevo), began to commission new genres such as frescoes, the bishop's portrait gallery and paintings of dignitaries lying in state, all of which became part of the Spalinszky brothers' oeuvre.

This full-figure icon of the Apostle Matthew was isolated from the iconostasis of painted Apostles, all of which were, presumably, after Baroque engravings and painted by the artist Mihály Spalinszky from Galitzia.

5d81f529-0519-5b10-ba1c-6c8d92b01735.name: The Battle between the Novgorodians and the Suzdalians
5d81f529-0519-5b10-ba1c-6c8d92b01735.description: This icon type, among the first to depict an event from Russian history, illustrates the 1169 battle in which the Suzdalians besieged the city of Novgorod. During the siege, Archbishop Ilya of Novgorod ordered that an icon of the Mother of God be brought out from the Church of the Transfiguration to give the Novgorodians courage. According to legend, the icon was displayed on the city walls where it was struck by a Suzdalian arrow. The icon miraculously began to weep, and through the intercession of the Mother of God, the Novgorodians defeated the Suzdalians. This image is particularly rich in its narrative and compositional details.
5d81f529-0519-5b10-ba1c-6c8d92b01735.obtention: Purchased by Gordon Lankton from a private collection in 1995. Gifted to the Museum of Russian Icons by Gordon Lankton in 2013.
keywords: Allegorical and symbolical figures; Virgin Mary and Child; Religious iconography

5e053a64-1076-5c13-b2f5-a260eeae41de.name:
The court of Kayumars  
Folio from the *Shahnameh* (Book of Kings) of Shah Tahmasp
5e053a64-1076-5c13-b2f5-a260eeae41de.short_description: Firdausi’s epic poem the *Shahnameh* (Book of Kings), completed in 1010, recounts the history of all of Iran’s shahs (kings) up to the Arab conquest in 642 AD and the country’s adoption of Islam. A large part of the poem focuses on prehistoric, legendary kings, some of whom ruled for hundreds of years and established man’s knowledge of everything from fire to weaving. According to Firdausi, the very idea of kingship originated with King Kayumars, who ruled for thirty years, overseeing a peaceable kingdom in which men wore leopard-skin robes and wild animals grew tame. In this utopia Kayumars had one secret enemy, the evil Ahriman, whose envy drove him to incite his own son, the Black Div, to murder Siyamak, the son of Kayumars. Before the assassination took place, the angel Surush warned Kayumars of Ahriman’s plot.
5e053a64-1076-5c13-b2f5-a260eeae41de.obtention: Former Prince Saddrudin Aga Khan Collection

5e51433f-c353-5de6-8d1d-14dc9459c3f2.name: *Moors of Tetouan*
5e51433f-c353-5de6-8d1d-14dc9459c3f2.description:
This painting was made around 1863 when the author travelled to Morocco with Mariano Fortuny. The reason for his travel was to paint the characters and picturesque garments as the way of life of the people from Morocco.  
His experiences can be seen in his paintings and drawings.  
During his travels he bought exotic artworks as Egyptian sarcophagi.  
Harem and markets are considered a genre painting in Orientalism.
5e51433f-c353-5de6-8d1d-14dc9459c3f2.author: Ámparo López
keywords: North Africa; Orientalism; Travelling

5f4d8280-c94a-5c7e-9533-fc8bc96f6c17.name: *The Blessed Franco Resurrecting a Child*
5f4d8280-c94a-5c7e-9533-fc8bc96f6c17.description:
This picture is part of a series hanging on three of the walls of the sacristy of the Carmelite church of Medicina, a town near Bologna. The cycle is well documented and so it is known exactly when each picture was hung on the wall. The attribution is certain: the architectural details were painted by Fra Ferdinando da Bologna, one of the best pupils of Ferdinando Bibiena. Originally, the figures were missing and the paintings were incomplete. In 1753, the Carmelite fathers asked the painter Nicola Bertuzzi from Ancona to complete Dal Buono architecture with the stories of the blessed Franco, who lived in the thirteenth-century.  
The picture of the *Miracle of the Resurrection of the Child* hangs above the entrance door of the sacristy. The scene takes place inside a great baroque church. The blessed Franco, with a penitential helmet on his head, answers the prayer of the little boy's mother and resuscitates him. The scene occupies the middle of the painting and is introduced by the wonder of a Carmelite brother, followed by a dog. The vivid description of the architectural details is made through a one-point corner perspective on the left. The luminosity of the central episode is emphasised by the dynamic lights and shades inside the scenography. In the background, Bertuzzi depicts some of the daily activities of the religious order such as confession and communion, that complete naturally the resurrection of the child. The culture of the Bibienas' is strongly evident, combined with the refined culture of Fra Ferdinando and the skilled work of Bertuzzi. The powerful scenic invention combines Bibienesque schemes with views of existing architecture reflective of the Carmelite Church of Medicina and the interior of the Cathedral of Ferrara. The decorative architecture, the vivid colours and the delicate lights are typical of a baroque taste moving towards Rococo.
5f4d8280-c94a-5c7e-9533-fc8bc96f6c17.short_description:
This painting was commissioned by the Carmelite community of Medicina in 1751 to the Bolognese painter Vincenzo Dal Buono also known as Fra’ Ferdinando da Bologna, a pupil of Ferdinando Bibiena. Nicola Bertuzzi added the stories of the blessed Franco at a later time.  
In the middle of the picture, the blessed, with the penitential helmet on his head, is resuscitating a child. The lively description of architecture is seen through a corner perspective with a vanishing point on the left, a typical feature of the Bibienas’.
5f4d8280-c94a-5c7e-9533-fc8bc96f6c17.owner: Parish church of San Mamante, Medicina

5ff60937-5e79-50fd-9f4b-b979480be0f5.name: *A Youth with a Lion* Folio from an album
5ff60937-5e79-50fd-9f4b-b979480be0f5.short_description:
The depicted scene takes place in a garden of a Persian Shah or a lord. Only the upper elite of Iranian society could afford keeping large predatory felines in their gardens. The young man's headdress fits the AD mid-17th century Safavid fashion.  
The author of the painting is Afzal al-Husayni (also named Mir Afzal Tuni, Afzal), a younger contemporary and follower of Reza Abbasi. Known primarily as the master of erotic drawing, Afzal preferred to depict the leisure of the Persian aristocracy: young men or love scenes in the garden. In addition to the artistic manner, the author is also indicated by an inscription in the bottom right of the folio that reads: “He! On the first day of the month of Jumat the Second of year 1056, the drawing of the most humble Afzal al-Husayni was completed”.  
Since the late 16th century the Iranian miniature has acquired the role of an independent piece of art. The prestige of the artist's work and his creative and economic freedom was growing, and it became much easier to make a living on producing single page works than on illustrating a whole book. Separate paintings as well as calligraphic folios with poems constituted *murakka* albums, reflecting the aesthetic and intellectual demand of wealthy collectors.

606d3d8f-c123-5583-829c-0f993f3625e5.name: *Still life with Crabs, Pitcher, Glass, Loaf and Mouse*
606d3d8f-c123-5583-829c-0f993f3625e5.description:
Izbighy Veres of Kassa (Košice) was one of the most accomplished painters of the period in Hungary. According to sources, he executed several commissions in Kassa (Košice), and a number of his still life paintings are in Slovakian and Hungarian collections today. Indications of the Hungarian origins of this painting are evident not only in the signature, but also in the blue-white lead-glazed jar; in addition, the loaf of bread is similar to that seen on a supraport painting by him in Koháry Castle at Szentantal (Antol). In another painting in the Xantus János Museum, Győr, Izbighy arranged a heap of crawfish on a plate in a similar way.  
Up until the beginning of the 20th century, discussion of Izbighy Veres' still life paintings was primarily in terms of their symbolic meaning. In this particular painting, however, this is hardly a major consideration as, clearly, it is influenced by the 17th-century still life genre of Austria and south Italy and, considering its style and spirituality, is certainly related to three works of the Austrian “Burgher paintress” Anna Maria Punz (Österreichische Galerie, Vienna), though this one by Izbighy is of an earlier date.
606d3d8f-c123-5583-829c-0f993f3625e5.short_description: The signed work of István Izbighy (Izbigi) Veres, a painter from Kassa (Košice) shows the influence of Austrian and south Italian still life painting, in particular the work of the “Burgher paintress” Anna Maria Punz. His other works may well have symbolic meaning but symbolism is a minor consideration when considering this particular painting.
606d3d8f-c123-5583-829c-0f993f3625e5.method_for_datation: The painting is signed and the date established by stylistic analysis.
606d3d8f-c123-5583-829c-0f993f3625e5.obtention: Transferred in an exchange from a Swiss private collection to a private collection in Karinthia, Austria.
606d3d8f-c123-5583-829c-0f993f3625e5.bibliography: Mojzer, M., (ed) “Cat. Nr. A. 44.” *The Metamorphosis of Themes: Secular Subjects in the Art of the Baroque in Central Europe, e*xhibition catalogue, Budapest, 1993.

keywords: Figural decoration; still life;  burgher; István Izbighy (Izbigi) Veres; Anna Maria Punz; southern Italy; Italian influence Kassa; Košice; Kaschau; Szentantal; Antol

60d42b24-3acf-5ae0-ab4f-e3aae453f313.name: *Still-life with Calligraphic Panel*
60d42b24-3acf-5ae0-ab4f-e3aae453f313.short_description: Feyhaman Duran was particularly interested in portrait painting and went to Paris in 1910 through the patronage of the Egyptian Prince Abbas Halim Pasha to further his studies in this genre. He greatly profited from the teaching of Paul Richet, professor of anatomy in the School of Fine Arts in Paris. He also attended the Julian Academy where he learned a great deal from Jean-Paul and Albert Laurens. In 1913-14 he worked in the Cormon studio in the School of Fine Arts. Although devoting most of his time to portrait painting, Feyhaman Duran also did paintings of flowers and nudes, but he was definitely most interested in the portrayal of people, and he had very little time for non-figurative painting.
keywords: Painting; Feyhaman Duran; orientalist painters; still life

60e1aa5c-a47e-5cdf-ab3b-bdba4f9694bd.name: *Perspective with a Banquet Scene*
60e1aa5c-a47e-5cdf-ab3b-bdba4f9694bd.description:
Ferdinando Bibiena was a great architect and scenographer. Working with his sons, Bibiena shared the artistic and theatrical Italian fashion of architectural perspective throughout Europe. In his last years he was a professor at the Accademia Clementina. His teachings promoted a predilection for perspective painting as an autonomous decorative genre that soon became very fashionable all over Europe.  
Bibiena painted this picture in 1721, upon returning to Bologna after a long stay in Vienna. There is a pendant of the same subject which was painted by a follower of Bibiena. Monumental architecture, arches, vaults, columns, and balustrades are on an angular perspective. Side vanishing points make the space deeper and convey the impression of a theatrical scene. The small figures taking part in the sumptuous banquet in the foreground come from different directions. They are positioned at the base of enormous columns, thus emphasising the magnificence of the architecture.
60e1aa5c-a47e-5cdf-ab3b-bdba4f9694bd.short_description: The painting was commissioned by the Accademia Clementina to Ferdinando Galli Bibiena in 1721. It was presented to the Senate of Bologna to celebrate the homecoming of the celebrated scenographer and theatrical architect and his congregation to the local Academy of fine arts. Magnificent architectural elements on an angular view form an eclectic and fantastic ensemble, the theatrical side of the baroque taste for illusion.
60e1aa5c-a47e-5cdf-ab3b-bdba4f9694bd.method_for_datation: Documents in the State Archive of Bologna show that the painting was already finished on the 6th of November 1721. The Accademia Clementina had already decided to have it delivered to the apartment of Gonfaloniere, on the first floor of Palazzo Comunale.
60e1aa5c-a47e-5cdf-ab3b-bdba4f9694bd.obtention: The painting, originally located on the first floor of Palazzo Comunale, was moved to the museum, on the second floor of the same building, in 1992.

6177d6e0-4105-5c92-a2c3-cf308dc051e6.name: "Alexander Fights a Sea Battle"
6177d6e0-4105-5c92-a2c3-cf308dc051e6.alternate_name: Folio from a Khamsa (Quintet) of Amir Khusrau Dihlavi
6177d6e0-4105-5c92-a2c3-cf308dc051e6.description: In the episode illustrated, Alexander the Great has ordered the construction of a tall tower surmounted by a revolving mirror in order to battle the pirates menacing the Mediterranean Sea. The protagonists appear as contemporary Indians wearing turbans and tunics, rather than ancient Greeks, and one of the fighters uses a gun, an invention from nearly two millennia after Alexander’s time.

61c3680d-7e1f-5627-a43b-1ebb99008f0e.name: Folio with two miniatures from Persian translation of 'The Wonders of Creation and the Oddities of Existence' by Zakaria Qazwini
61c3680d-7e1f-5627-a43b-1ebb99008f0e.short_description: A folio from Persian translation of a popular cosmography treatise "The Wonders of Creation and the Oddities of Existence" by Zakaria bin Muhammad al-Qazwini. The book, written in AD 13th century, covers the fields of geography, astronomy, astrology and natural history, in a mixture of science and superstition. Both sides of the folio are embellished with miniatures featuring fruit-bearing trees.

6204d094-907f-5ef3-b378-936a43e07247.name: An Entertainment Scene (The third day of entertainment) from *Surname-i Vehbi*
6204d094-907f-5ef3-b378-936a43e07247.short_description: These images show events that took place on the Golden Horn on the evening of the third day. In them, we see the sultan seated in a tent on the Arsenal Palace quay surrounded by attendants. Two rafts are floating by. The one at the right, of which we can only see a part but appears to be a platform mounted on a pair of caiques, was donated by Yeğen Mehmed Pasha, Superintendent of the Customs Office. The figures of two rams suspended on gears and pulleys from the roof butt one another. This is following a real raft on which are set two gigantic dummies that face backwards and are dressed in Persian garb. At the front of the raft is a huge wheel of fireworks that one of the pyrotechnicists is causing to revolve. Its supporting frame is surmounted by a fire-spewing bird and rockets hurtle this way and that.
keywords: Levni; miniature; entertainment; Dance

643bea8a-60c4-536d-8abb-76054e8cc2b2.name: *Holy Family with Saints John and Elizabeth*
643bea8a-60c4-536d-8abb-76054e8cc2b2.description:
Nothing is known of the date nor who commissioned the painting, first recorded in the collection of Scipione Borghese in 1650. It is, therefore, likely that it may originally have been linked to the Cardinal. Pulzone had painted a portrait of his uncle Camillo, who became Pope in 1605, forging strong links with the noble family.  
The canvas is one of the most celebrated paintings of the Counter-Reformation, practically its thesis. A moral interpretation of its subject contrasts the motherhood of the young Mary with the characteristics of the aged Elizabeth. Indeed their gestures clearly express the virtues that distinguish them: modesty and chastity for Mary, patience and benevolence for Elizabeth.  
This was one of the first works to be completed in accordance with the dictates of the Council of Trent. Although it is not dominated by a rigid structure, the devotional emphases linked to the spirituality of the time, of which Pulzone was one of the great exponents, has a great sensitivity. Here the artist combines Flemish detail with his predilection for the careful representation of reality, the Venetian colour he found through Sebastiano Luciani (“Sebastiano del Piombo”) and careful drafting, of which he is a master.  
His enormous capacity to assimilate different styles and intentions are fused into this fundamental work, which can be dated between 1588 and 1590, during which time he was active on an important project at the Gesù Church site where he worked with the famous Jesuit Giuseppe Valeriano.  
The artist also worked for the Congregation of the Oratory of St. Philip Neri. The composition of the work is extremely simple; the figures arranged using criteria from the 15th century. The most significant comparison is with the work of Raphael, which can be seen in the expression of the characters, whose figures assume a highly monumental character.
643bea8a-60c4-536d-8abb-76054e8cc2b2.short_description: Pulzone, one of the leading painters of the Counter-Reformation, was particularly active for the new religious orders, such as the Oratory founded by St. Filippo Neri. He is also well known as a portrait painter.
643bea8a-60c4-536d-8abb-76054e8cc2b2.obtention: The Borghese Collection was acquired by the Italian State in 1902.

649d4fc6-efad-5c54-848f-c9739373ad0f.name: *The Elephant Clock*, folio from a *Book of the Knowledge of Ingenious Mechanical Devices* by al-Jazari
649d4fc6-efad-5c54-848f-c9739373ad0f.short_description: This folio comes from a treatise on fantastic devices invented by the author Isma‘il al-Jazari. His elephant clock was especially intricate: every half hour, the bird on the dome whistled, the man below dropped a ball into the dragon’s mouth, and the driver hit the elephant with his goad. This automaton is reminiscent of the elaborate clocks found on medieval town halls in Europe, which made the passage of time more entertaining through the performance of the moving figures. The folio is a rare survival from Syria, where few such manuscripts from this date are known.

656be3c6-61c1-54ad-b1d9-a2b1dcaa12a9.name: Nature morte à la corbeille de verres et aux roses blanches
656be3c6-61c1-54ad-b1d9-a2b1dcaa12a9.short_description:
This is a still life consisting of a basket of glasses, a present-day picture postcard of Romont Castle, an empty lemonade bottle with the label “Fribourg” and a vase of white roses. A rose branch with a shoot and a withered petal lies next to it. The basket covers the upper edge of a postcard lying underneath, on which a biblical scene (the healing of Tobias) appears.  
  
The work consists of glass with facet cut. It was created for the inauguration of the permanent exhibition of reverse glass at the Vitromusée Romont in October 2006, when the museum was renovated and its collection extended to include not only stained glass but glass art in general. Two compositional elements reference this context: the postcard of Romont Castle, which houses the museum, and the postcard depicting a reverse painting on glass by Swiss artist Franz Thaddäus Menteler the Younger (1751–94) from 1780. The glass basket is also a reference to the 17th-century Alsatian Mannerist Sébastien Stoskopff.  
  
The painting is notable for the delicate light effects on the glasses and the play between translucence and reflection of the vase and bottle. In Yves Siffer’s work, almost all the objects depicted recall human activities and evoke everyday life. His still life works are often allegories of transience.
